summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 6 upside misses — ACN +6%, IBM +6%, GNRC +5%, CAG +5%, PWR +5%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (SNDK -14%, MU -12%, ON -10%, VRT -10%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: SNDK (-14.02%) — SK Hynix announced a Nasdaq ADR listing (July 10, raising ~$29.4B), eroding SNDK's scarcity premium as the sole US pure-play AI-memory stock; compounded by second-day KOSPI/Samsung/SK Hynix contagion selloff (-10% KOSPI, -12% each). Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe — SNDK's ~$1,981 price and ~79x P/E after a 5,000% post-spin-off run likely breach universe filters (per-share price cap, vol ceiling, or float/liquidity thresholds). The SK Hynix ADR catalyst also required pre-open short positioning before US signals formed.

top_movers.catalyst: Accenture raised FY2026 buybacks by $2B to $7.5B on June 23, signaling management views shares as undervalued following the stock's ~17% drop on June 18 on weak Q3 bookings and trimmed guidance.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe; ACN is a large-cap IT services stock. Post-earnings buyback-bounce moves require event-driven fundamental coverage — momentum and mean-reversion algos screen out stocks down ~17% in the prior week.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a buyback-expansion event gate: if a stock files an 8-K announcing ≥$1B repurchase increase within 5 sessions of a ≥10% earnings gap-down, trigger a mean-reversion long with 3-day max hold for liquid large-caps.

top_movers.catalyst: JPMorgan upgraded IBM to Overweight (PT $270→$291) citing software's ~66% profit contribution; IBM simultaneously joined OpenAI's Daybreak Cyber program and received White House quantum endorsement at an Oval Office ceremony.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — IBM is a mega-cap Dow component excluded from typical momentum screens. Move was triggered by a post-close analyst upgrade (June 23), requiring pre-open positioning that reactive signal scanners cannot capture.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a Tier-1 analyst-upgrade event gate: when a major bank issues an Overweight upgrade with ≥7% price-target raise on a large-cap name before market open, admit the name into the news-reactive strategy's universe for that session only.

top_movers.catalyst: Jefferies upgraded GNRC Hold→Buy (PT $302 from $239) citing data center contract conversion opportunities, layering onto the June 2 hyperscale supply-agreement announcement and AI infrastructure tailwind.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — GNRC is a NYSE mid/large-cap C&I industrial (~$7B+ market cap, power generation equipment). Move was analyst-upgrade-driven, with the gap priced in pre-market before any reactive signal could fire.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a catalyst-upgrade tier that scans for ≥2-notch analyst upgrades (Hold→Buy) on NYSE industrials with new PT implying ≥10% upside, gated by pre-market volume ≥1.5× 30-day avg, to enter within the first 30 minutes of open.

top_movers.catalyst: Pre-earnings re-rating ahead of July 15 Q4 FY2026 report; new CEO John Brase (installed June 1) + Q3 2.4% organic sales growth fueling turnaround confidence in a heavily sold-off consumer staples name.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — CAG was demoted to S&P SmallCap 600 after steep YoY declines (~-32%), falling below large/mid-cap universe thresholds. The move was gradual pre-earnings sentiment drift, not an overnight gap or volume spike catchable by momentum filters.
top_movers.suggestion: Expand universe to include former S&P 500/400 names now in SmallCap 600 within 21 days of earnings showing positive organic-revenue trend; apply standard liquidity floor (≥$5M ADTV) to gate entry.

top_movers.catalyst: No fresh Jun 24 catalyst found; technical snap-back from Jun 23's -5.1% pullback, continuing Jun 22 momentum from Hyosung HICO high-voltage circuit-breaker JV and raised FY2026 revenue guidance ($34.7B–$35.2B).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. PWR is a ~$112B large-cap industrial EPC contractor trading near $739/share — likely excluded by sector scope (Industrials/grid-services EPC not covered) or a per-share price ceiling rather than any technical filter.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a grid-infrastructure sector sleeve to the momentum strategy (market cap ≥ $10B, sub-sector = Electrical Contractors/EPC) and raise the per-share price ceiling to $1,000 to include names like PWR.

top_movers.catalyst: Erie Insurance rose 15 spots to #308 on the 2026 Fortune 500 list, signalling franchise strength; bounce amplified by technical recovery near the 52-week low ($205) after a -22.7% YTD drawdown.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. ERIE is a mid-cap P&C insurer with only 3 sell-side analysts and negative YTD momentum (-22.7%); likely misses liquidity floors and momentum signal thresholds on all universe screens.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a mean-reversion sub-universe for P&C insurers with a JD Power top-5 ranking, >15% YTD drawdown, and avg daily dollar volume >$8M; trigger entry on days the KIE ETF rises ≥0.5%.

top_movers.catalyst: SK Hynix announced a Nasdaq ADR listing (July 10, raising ~$29.4B), eroding SNDK's scarcity premium as the sole US pure-play AI-memory stock; compounded by second-day KOSPI/Samsung/SK Hynix contagion selloff (-10% KOSPI, -12% each).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — SNDK's ~$1,981 price and ~79x P/E after a 5,000% post-spin-off run likely breach universe filters (per-share price cap, vol ceiling, or float/liquidity thresholds). The SK Hynix ADR catalyst also required pre-open short positioning before US signals formed.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a competitor-listing catalyst rule: when a direct sub-sector rival announces a US ADR/IPO ≥$5B, flag the incumbent pure-play proxy for a short entry within 30 minutes of open, gated on prior-session beta ≥1.5 vs SOX.

top_movers.catalyst: SK Hynix disclosed an HBM4 capacity slowdown (shifting production to conventional DRAM), sparking sector-wide AI memory demand fears; compounded by pre-earnings profit-taking ahead of MU's own Q3 report due after today's close.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — likely excluded by mega-cap size (~$1.2T mkt cap at prior close). The drop was competitor-driven sector contagion from an SK Hynix capacity disclosure, not a MU-specific technical or fundamental signal.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a semiconductor sector-contagion watch: when a top-3 memory peer (SK Hynix, Samsung) files a capacity-shift disclosure, automatically flag in-universe chip names for a momentum short entry within 30 minutes of the news crossing wires.

top_movers.catalyst: Broad semiconductor sector profit-taking after a sharp recent rally (BofA/WF raised targets to $138-140 signaling peak sentiment); no ON-specific negative news — AI/EV power tailwinds intact but valuation stretched ~14% above models.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. ON is a $26B large-cap pure-play semiconductor (NASDAQ) — likely excluded by a sector or universe filter. The move was sector-rotation driven, not a momentum/mean-reversion signal; pre-position would have required shorting into an extended rally.
top_movers.suggestion: Add top-10 semiconductor names (ON, MCHP, MPWR) to a sector-momentum overlay: when SOXX ETF drops ≥3% over 2 sessions and individual name is +20% over prior 30 days, flag for short entry — captures stretched-valuation sector unwinds without broad universe expansion.

top_movers.catalyst: Macro AI-sector contagion: South Korea's financial regulator flagged leveraged chip-fund risks (Samsung/SK Hynix), sparking a broad AI-infrastructure sell-off that dragged VRT ~9.6% with no company-specific news.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. The drop was pure macro contagion — no earnings, no filing, no pre-market signal — making pre-open positioning impossible. VRT's ~175% prior-year run and ~83× forward P/E also place it above typical momentum-strategy valuation ceilings.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a macro-shock mean-reversion scan: when an AI-infrastructure proxy ETF (e.g. GRID) falls ≥3% intraday on no single-stock catalyst, auto-flag high-beta correlated names for next-open fade entries, gated to names with 90-day return ≥50% to target the most stretched.
